question: On 15 July 2026, the Member States agreed to extend temporary protection for Ukrainian nationals until 4 March 2028. The mechanism, intended as an exceptional and temporary solution, will by then have been in force for six years. According to Eurostat, in May 2026, 4.38 million people were benefiting from it in the EU, including 967 505 in Poland. Poland had 26.

5 beneficiaries per 1 000 inhabitants, compared with an EU average of 9.7. This temporary arrangement cannot continue indefinitely. Beneficiaries should transition to standard residence permits or international protection assessed on a case-by-case basis. 1.

Does the Commission intend to bring collective protection to a definitive end on 4 March 2028 and to transition its beneficiaries to standard residence permits or international protection assessed on a case-by-case basis; if not, what binding deadline and what measurable criteria for termination does it intend to propose?

Why does the requirement to demonstrate compliance with Ukrainian military obligations apply only to new applicants, and is the Commission considering reassessing current beneficiaries in connection with the extension of protection until 2028?
